Involves multiple Th2 derived cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-9, IL-10), but current therapies are limited by their activity on a subset of these cytokines.
ITK (interleukin-2 inducible T cell kinase) is expressed by T cells and is involved in both T cell receptor signaling and differentiation of naïve T cells into Th2 cells.

Inhibition of ITK preferentially reduces the synthesis of Th2-derived cytokines including IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13. CPI-818 is an oral, selective drug that binds covalently to ITK to inhibit its enzymatic function.

It is being evaluated in a single agent, dose-escalation phase 1 trial in patients with refractory T cell lymphoma and demonstrates anti- tumor activity along with evidence of reduction of Th2 cell differentiation and Th2 cytokine production.
We have evaluated CPI-818 in spontaneous canine AD (CAD) as a model for human disease.
Five dogs with recurrent, moderate to severe CAD were treated with CPI-818 at a dose of 10 to 20 mg/kg BID for up to 28 days.
Primary efficacy outcomes were the PVAS (pruritus visual analog scale) and CADLI (canine atopic dermatitis lesion index).
All dogs had improvement in the PVAS within 2 days of starting CPI-818.
Four dogs were evaluable for at least 14 days and showed improvement in PVAS (32 + 16%) (mean + SD).
Improvement on Day 28 in PVAS was 34 + 22%.
Three of 4 dogs had an improved CADLI on Day 14 and all had improved CADLI (20 + 10% )on Day 28.
One dog, whose PVAS on Day 9 had improved 45%, withdrew from study for suspected drug rash; no serious adverse events were encountered.
This CAD trial demonstrates that ITK inhibition may represent a novel approach to treatment of atopic diseases with the potential advantage of inhibiting the production of multiple Th2 cytokines.
